top.title: ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye May Edochie, the estranged wife of Pete Edochie’s son Yul, has mourned the veteran actor, calling him “an institution” whose legacy will live on. In a glowing tribute shared on Instagram on Wednesday, May recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death had circulated over the years, but he had continued working. Pete’s family announced that he died in Enugu at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. “For so many years, every year, someone somewhere makes a false announcement of your death but you kept going with strength to continue working,” she wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by May Yul-Edochie (@mayyuledochie) Reflecting on his death, May said: “One moment, there is life; the next, eternity calls. Such is the fragility of human existence. We make plans, hold conversations, nurse expectations and believe there will always be another day, until life reminds us that tomorrow is never promised.” Calling him the “Lion of Africa,” she said his passing reminded her that “beyond all, the opinions, the misunderstandings and the stories that life sometimes throws around, we are all humans, and death has a way of reminding us of what truly matters.” May also said she would remember Pete as a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contributions to Nollywood would remain unforgettable. “You were an institution, a father figure to many and a man whose legacy will outlive his earthly years,” she wrote. “One thing is certain: legends never truly die; they live on through the memories they create and the impact they leave behind.” She also prayed for Pete’s wife, Josephine, and other relatives, writing: “To mummy and the rest of us you have left behind, may the good Lord strengthen through Christ our Lord.” She ended the tribute with prayers for the deceased: “God rest your soul Ononenyi!” Vanguard News The post ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law
top.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them. The comedian made the remarks during an appearance on the Charity Zone Podcast, where he argued that the benefits of some government policies might take years to become evident. Seyi Law, a known supporter of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), said economic policies often come with immediate difficulties before producing long term gains. Using China as an example, he said the country’s emergence as a major global economy involved significant sacrifices. “For China to be where they are today, if they tell you the number of Chinese who died, you won’t believe,” he said. When asked whether Nigerians must die before enjoying the benefits of the country’s economic policies, the comedian clarified that people would have to experience the hardship resulting from such decisions before the expected gains could materialise. “No. You must feel the pain of the policy to reap the benefit of it. Every good policy that becomes good stabilises after 10 to 12 years,” he said. Despite his defence of the government, Seyi Law acknowledged the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians, admitting that people were struggling to afford basic necessities. “People are hungry. I will be a hypocrite, a bad person to say people are not hungry,” he said. He also spoke about how the rising cost of living had affected his ability to support family members living in the United Kingdom. According to him, an amount that previously covered their needs now requires a significantly higher sum, forcing him to increase his financial support. “My finances were better before this government came in. My family are in the UK and then with N1.2 million they are okay, but now I have had to double that to like N4.5 million every other month,” he added. top.title: Braves Lefty Suter Signs $4 Million Deal With Yankees
top.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Relief pitcher Brent Suter is heading to New York. The left-hander, who pitched well for the Braves late in the 2026 season, signed a one-year contract worth $4 million with the Yankees. This move ends his time in Atlanta and adds a proven arm to the Bronx Bombers’ bullpen. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported the deal on Tuesday, confirming Suter will not return to the team that traded for him in August. Suter arrived at the trade deadline from the Angels in exchange for infielder Nacho Alvarez Jr. He made an immediate impact with the Braves, posting a 2-0 record and a 1.63 ERA across 13 regular season games. His work did not stop there. During the National League Division Series versus the Dodgers, he also played in two contests, pitching three scoreless innings. Despite these strong numbers, the Braves chose not to keep him for the 2027 season. A Reluctant Loss for Atlanta The Braves have seen this before. Suter is now the first notable free agent from the 2026 roster to sign elsewhere. Other pitchers like Tyler Mahle and Martín Pérez remain unsigned, along with infielder Mauricio Dubón and closer Raisel Iglesias. However, losing a lefty with Suter’s recent track record hurts. He was a steady hand in high-leverage spots when the team needed him most. The decision to let him walk suggests the front office is looking to save money or believes other arms are ready to step up. Either way, the Yankees just gained a player who knows how to get outs in the playoffs. The $4 million price tag reflects his value. It is a fair sum for a veteran lefty who can eat innings and keep the ball in the park. The Yankees are known for spending to fill gaps, and this signing fits their pattern. They needed depth after a long season, and Suter provides exactly that. For Atlanta, the loss is not just about the numbers. It is about the stability he offered in a bullpen that often gets tested. The team now has to find someone else to fill that role without the benefit of Suter’s experience. The NL East Shifts Again The division is getting harder to navigate. While the Braves lose Suter, the New York Mets are making massive moves of their own. Tarik Skubal signed a record nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets, according to Yahoo Sports . top.title: What Peugeot had planned for its abandoned 2027 WEC Hypercar
top.description: Motorsport photo The 2027-spec 9X8 LMH was set to offer Peugeot its best chance of becoming a consistent World Endurance Championship frontrunner against some stiff Hypercar competition. The French manufacturer had invested considerable resources into developing a revised version of the car that had fallen short of the expectations set by its predecessor, the 908 LMP1. This would have been the third major iteration of the V6-powered challenger, following a previous update in 2024 that failed to yield the desired results. By mid-2025, Peugeot had already identified several key weaknesses with the package. Even after being granted the lowest weight and the maximum power under the Balance of Performance adjustments, the 9X8 was simply not competitive enough against the likes of Toyota, Porsche and Ferrari . Peugeot felt that incremental refinements alone would not be enough, with the car having reached a performance ceiling that engineers struggled to overcome. While Peugeot initially considered ditching the 9X8 entirely in favour of a clean-sheet design, even holding talks with the WEC’s promoters – to understand if this would be allowed, it eventually chose to update its existing car instead. The French manufacturer had its hands tied in 2026, having already exhausted its original allocation of five evo jokers and the second homologation. So it spent the year struggling largely at the back of the pack, while its engineers simultaneously began working on overhauling the package for 2027, with a new rule granting struggling manufacturers two additional evo updates during their cars' life cycles. Crucially, the update Peugeot had planned for 2027 wasn’t about undoing the damage caused by the convergence of the LMH and LMDh regulations – something that had significantly compromised the original design of the car. Instead, it was aimed at tackling the specific shortcomings of the second-generation 9X8, including its notoriously poor performance at the Le Mans 24 Hours. As with other manufacturers introducing evo updates, aerodynamics was the key focus of development for the Satory-based brand. But it was also working on several other changes under the hood to improve the cornering performance of the 9X8. #94 Peugeot Totalenergies Peugeot 9X8: Loic Duval #94 Peugeot Totalenergies Peugeot 9X8: Loic Duval “In terms of development of the car, the key targets were to eradicate the issues we had with the current package,” team principal Emmanuel Esnault explained at Monza earlier this month. “So, meaning in terms of [aero] dumping [to improve straightline performance] and in terms of aero consistency; these were the key words. “The main handicaps we had were the aerodynamic balance variation on the three phases that make up a corner; that is the entry, the middle of the corner and the exit. “And the [other area of focus was] control of the platform, which is the damping of the suspension. top.title: Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football. In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario that he had spoken with the Italian Football Federation but was not ready to take another job. “It was one of the greatest honours I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop,” he said. “If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted.” The Spaniard said the approach came when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom he described as people he loved dearly, reached out to him. He added that he did not know how long his break would last. “Right now I feel very well,” Guardiola told former Brazil forward Romario. “But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.” Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after a decade in charge. He won six Premier League titles, including four in succession, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League. In the same interview, Guardiola said Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry helped prolong both players’ careers. The pair won a combined 13 Ballon d’Or awards and dominated football for more than a decade, including during their spells at Barcelona and Real Madrid. “If Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter,” Guardiola said. “They had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him,’” Guardiola, who coached Messi for four seasons at Barcelona, credited the forward for much of his success there. He led the Spanish club to 14 trophies, including two Champions League titles and three La Liga crowns. “Messi! When you have such good players, you become good yourself,” Guardiola said when asked what helped him win so many titles. top.title: Confirmed: Fermin Lopez hit with two-match ban; will miss Deportivo, Atletico Madrid games
top.description: Confirmed: Fermin Lopez hit with two-match ban; will miss Deportivo, Atletico Madrid games In what comes as a blow for Barcelona, key midfielder Fermin Lopez has been hit with a two-match suspension following his red card against Villarreal last Sunday. As a result, the in-form 23-year-old will miss the team’s La Liga matches against Deportivo de A Coruna and Atletico Madrid over the coming week. What happened? Fermin was sent off by referee Hernandez Hernandez while being seated on the Barcelona bench in the second half during the 3-2 win over Villarreal. It emanated from the La Masia graduate, who had scored on the day before being subbed off, voicing his protest over a potential penalty decision not going the Catalans’ way for a foul on Anthony Gordon. Fermin was sent off against Villarreal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The referee recorded the incident in his report, stating that the midfielder had left the dugout and approached the fourth official at close range while protesting loudly. The referee specifically noted that Fermin repeatedly used the expression “Don’t f**k with me!” during the exchange. Two-match ban Barcelona were hoping that the youngster would get away with only a one-match suspension. However, the Disciplinary Committee has classified the incident as a protest under Article 127 of the Disciplinary Code. The regulation provides for a suspension of between two and three matches, or a ban of up to one month, for protesting against the referee, assistant referees or fourth official when the conduct does not constitute a more serious offence. Two-match ban for Fermin. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Fermin has now received the minimum suspension under the article: two matches. Barcelona had submitted an appeal in an attempt to challenge the decision, but they were not accepted. The suspension means the midfielder will be unavailable for Barcelona’s visit to Deportivo at Riazor this Sunday. The more significant absence comes next Wednesday, when Barcelona host Atletico Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou – a fixture that was initially scheduled for January but brought forward due to the Spanish Super Cup scheduling. Barcelona have little room to challenge the decision successfully through the Appeals Committee as the disciplinary body has imposed the lowest punishment available under the relevant regulation, which makes the prospect of reducing the suspension limited. Source: Mundo Deportivo

top.title: Cut the Grass: After Mexico City, the 49ers Get Back to Work in the NFC West
top.description: On December 1, 2001, my Bowie High School team beat Eleanor Roosevelt 23-6 at Byrd Stadium for the first state championship in school history. We were the sixth seed. Roosevelt was undefeated and had beaten us in September. They had won nine straight against us, going back to 1994. We scored the first 23 points. When it was over, one of my teammates walked off that field with a plastic bag full of grass—a souvenir. I got home late that night. My parents were proud, but they kept it simple: Be safe, and be home when we wake up. The next morning, I was in church. I even got a shout-out from the pulpit. And that afternoon, I was in the yard cutting the grass, because the playoff run had put me behind on my chores. Took me years to understand it, but the trophy and the lawnmower were the same lesson. The habits that won the championship were the same ones that had me cutting grass the next day. Sunday night in Mexico City was the 49ers’ championship night. A 35-10 win over the best defense in football, in prime time, on an international stage. By Monday, they were Super Bowl favorites, and Brock Purdy’s MVP odds had jumped from +400 to +210. Then Kyle Shanahan was asked if this is the best team he’s coached in San Francisco. “No, but it’s still early,” he said. “We’ve got to earn that.” Now it’s back to the yard. It’s been 49 days since the 49ers played a division game, and the last one took just about everything they had. Seven turnovers between the two teams. Six lead changes. The 49ers hadn’t scored a touchdown against Seattle in more than eight quarters until Mike Evans caught a 2-yarder less than four minutes in. Renardo Green picked off Sam Darnold twice. Fred Warner punched a ball loose, Malik Mustapha fell on it, and Christian McCaffrey scored on the next snap. With 13 seconds left in the half, G-Baby, rookie Gracen Halton, stripped George Holani and recovered it in the end zone. Then Seattle scored 13 straight in the third quarter, and the 49ers had to go get it. Down 26-21, they went 74 yards in 12 plays, and Evans caught a 28-yarder on second-and-21 to set up the go-ahead touchdown. The winning field goal came at the end of a drive built on five runs for 36 yards, and Seattle’s last shot died when Cooper Kupp came up short on fourth-and-10 at midfield. top.title: Man behind the curtain calling entertainment plays at Polar Park
top.description: WORCESTER – While fans watch the players sweep through the field, sing along to classics and new hits, and wait for their sick moves to appear on the jumbotron, there is a man sitting behind a curtain making it all happen. Actually, there are several. Many people go to the ballpark to watch the game, but it is not the only interesting thing happening there. From music to the kiss cam, the Worcester Red Sox Entertainment Department helps turn baseball into a full night out at Polar Park. Without the technology that has become a regular part of the modern-day ballpark experience, this job would look significantly different. Before video boards became a regular feature, scoreboards were used for the minimum: the score, the inning and the lineup. That changed in 1980 when Dodger Stadium introduced the first full-color video board during the All-Star Game. This technology opened up new opportunities for entertainment beyond the game. Over time, video boards brought replays, highlights, promotional videos and crowd-participation features. According to Fun While it Lasted, a website that documents the history of sports, when the Pawtucket Red Sox – rebranded as the Worcester Red Sox – moved to Worcester in 2021, the franchise significantly stepped up its technology game. Polar Park was built with five boards, including two large video screens. It was a huge change from McCoy Stadium, which had been referred to as “a dump” by Ben Mondor, a retired mill owner who became the Pawtucket Red Sox’s third owner in the '70s. Westborough native at the controls For Brendan Black, a longtime baseball fan who grew up in Westborough, those large screens were wildly important. He is the director of ballpark entertainment. Black began working for the team in 2021 as a videographer before moving into a producer role in 2023. His job took root at age 10, when he was first interested in photography and videography, eventually teaching himself how to edit videos. After studying communications at the University of New Hampshire, he found himself working in sales to pay the bills. It was a relief when the WooSox came along, opening up an opportunity for him. “It just so happened that these two worlds of mine kind of collided,” Black said, recalling what it was like to bring together two interests that had followed him for years – baseball and entertainment. But putting on a show takes more than making a playlist and pressing "play." On game days, the work begins long before the fans fill the seats. At 10 a.m., the team holds what Black calls a “DOG” meeting – short for Day of Game. The staff goes over the weather, expected crowd size, ticket blocks and any promotions planned. top.title: John Motson’s legendary voice resurrected by AI for EA FC 27
top.description: Legendary football commentator John Motson‘s voice is set to return to EA FC 27 through the use of AI - three years after his death. Motson, who died aged 77 in 2023 , worked on the BBC ’s flagship Match of the Day programme since 1971 and covered more than 2,000 televised games, including 29 FA Cup finals and 10 World Cups. He retired from live commentary in 2008 but continued to work on Match of the Day programme until he hung up the microphone in 2018. EA Sports said they worked with John Motson’s family to bring back his iconic voice in a “digital tribute” through the use of new AI-tools, “bringing a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself”. The commentator featured in EA Sports’ annual FIFA game series from 1996 to 2006. John Motson featured in EA Sports’ annual FIFA game series from 1996 to 2006 A studio spokesperson said EA Sports have “worked with extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game’s greatest voices, inspiring a whole new generation of football fans.” “My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,” said Fred Motson, son of John Motson. “His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.” After starting as a newspaper reporter in Barnet and at the Sheffield Morning Telegraph , Motson joined the BBC in 1968 as a sports presenter on Radio 2. His long career also took in two Olympic Games and Wimbledon’s memorable 1988 FA Cup final triumph against Liverpool at Wembley, as the Crazy Gang beat the Culture Club. Awarded the OBE in 2001 for services to broadcasting, Motson hung up his microphone for the BBC at the end of the 2017-18 Premier League season. top.title: Charley Hull brings laughs, nerves and a wink to highly anticipated WTGL debut
top.description: PALM BEACH GARDENS, Fla. — Atlanta Drive's Charley Hull stood in a bunker at SoFi Center holding a conversation with team owner Arthur Blank. Hull, whose team would make its WTGL debut about 30 minutes later, then grabbed her wedge, and as Blank was walking away, holed a 30-footer. Looking on and nodding with approval was Billy Horschel, a star on Atlanta's TGL team. For Hull — and Atlanta — that proved to be the highlight of the night. Even with Horschel and Justin Thomas, both part of Atlanta's championship winning team in TGL's inaugural season, lending support from the team owner's box, Boston Common Golf defeated Atlanta, 8-3, Tuesday at SoFi Center. Boston Common had the advantage of playing its second WTGL match. "Obviously it wasn't the result that we wanted, but we had a great laugh," Hull said in perhaps the most upbeat post-game press conference ever held by a losing team. "It is a lot of fun. It's nice actually to be ... I know we're not on the golf course, but you're in the golf environment, and having a laugh." Hull, one of the marquee names playing in WTGL's first season, is considered the most popular active women's golfer in Europe. The Englishwoman is No. 7 in the world, a three-time winner on the LPGA Tour and although she still is chasing her first major championship, she has five runner-ups in the tour's marquee events. She has played in eight Solheim Cups. Hull, 30, also this year checked off what she called a childhood dream, appearing in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit edition. All of which makes her a natural for a league that encourages the golfers to let loose and show their personality. Her 869,000 Instagram followers are more than any other golfer on WTGL's 25-woman roster. "I think it's cool that here in WTGL we can expose people that it's actually fun to play golf and dress pretty cool," said Hull's teammate, Nataliya Guseva. "I think that's kind of our goal as well with Charley out here with the Malbon (golf fashion) stuff." Every woman who has played in the league's first four matches agrees the league is part entertainment and fashion along with the competition. Guseva, the 23-year-old Russian, had a rough night, drawing three penalties. She admitted to having nerves and said ... well, here is what she said. "It was super cool, but it was just kind of weird ... to show how nervous I am," she said. "But at the same time, every golfer kind of has nerves, and I think it's kind of cool to show that even professional golfers kind of s*** themselves during a tournament." "Yeah, I think it was great." Charley Hull's WTGL debut: A lot of laughs in Atlanta's loss From the entertainment side, Hull's debut was as expected. top.title: Penn State offense, Maryland defense are evenly matched
top.description: This has been a challenging season for Penn State’s offense to say the least. Instead of a consistently productive unit that improved as the season went along, they’ve presented a disjointed operation that excels one week and is left searching for answers the next week. The ebbs and flows of the season have been aggressive, even in individual games. A staple of the Nittany Lions offense has been jumping out to double-digit leads in the first half, and then completely falling apart in the second half, whether it be from turnovers or just a lack of execution. Maryland doesn’t have a great defense, but Penn State recently showed that even the worst defenses — like the Rutgers Scarlet Knights — can have success against it. The offense for the blue and white could score 40 points this week, or they could barely hit 20 points and be in a dog fight late in the fourth quarter. It’s impossible to know which version of the Nittany Lions will show up from week to week, but here are the raw numbers about the unit compared to the Terrapins defense. Turnovers Penn State offense: 9 turnovers Maryland defense: 15 takeaways Turnovers have the biggest indicator of whether Penn State will win this season. The team is 6-0 when it doesn’t turn the ball over, and 5-0 when it turns the ball over at all. The Nittany Lions have been one of the best teams in terms of taking care of the ball, currently tied for 18th in the nation with just nine giveaways. However, Maryland ranks in the top-third of college football with 15 takeaways. Linebacker Daniel Wingate has accounted for 20% of those all by himself, so Penn State needs to put an extreme focus on holding onto the ball this week. Passing yards per game Penn State offense: 232.5 Maryland defense: 216.4 Penn State’s passing game hasn’t been without its struggles this season, but it also has been the most reliable means of moving the ball. The air attack is above average nationally, currently ranking 59th out of all FBS teams with 232.5 yards per game. Maryland’s defense is middle of the pack in this category, ranking 75th with 216.4 yards allowed per game. That is the range the defense falls in for most categories. This means that the Terrapins aren’t great on that side of the ball, but they also aren’t a pushover. Rocco Becht will have to be on his A-game on Saturday because one slip up will likely be the game. He has to play a clean game and air the ball out efficiently against Maryland like many other quarterbacks have this year. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . top.title: Braves Free Agent Drawing Interest From Orioles After Career Year
top.description: Free agent utilityman Mauricio Dubon The Baltimore Orioles signed Freddy Peralta to a five-year, $125 million deal, but they may not be done adding to their team. The Orioles could use some help on offense, and according to The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , they are showing interest in Mauricio Dubón, among other players. Dubón is an interesting target for any team. He is a versatile defender who can play all over the field and is coming off a career year with the bat. The big question, however, is whether he can continue being a force at the plate. He set career highs in hits, RBIs, extra-base hits, walks and on-base percentage. He won his third career Gold Glove Award. He has had one other season where he was this good offensively, and it came in 2023 with the Houston Astros. The Orioles could use Dubón in the outfield, or as an option at second base if Jackson Holliday cannot figure things out. Regardless, players in Dubón's tier of free agents are where the Orioles should be expected to shop. He is 32 years old and may not get a long-term deal. However, he is the type of player a team needs to win a championship. He is a reliable utilityman who plays plus defense. He is also regarded as a great presence in the clubhouse. nigeria.title: ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye May Edochie, the estranged wife of Pete Edochie’s son Yul, has mourned the veteran actor, calling him “an institution” whose legacy will live on. In a glowing tribute shared on Instagram on Wednesday, May recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death had circulated over the years, but he had continued working. Pete’s family announced that he died in Enugu at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. “For so many years, every year, someone somewhere makes a false announcement of your death but you kept going with strength to continue working,” she wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by May Yul-Edochie (@mayyuledochie) Reflecting on his death, May said: “One moment, there is life; the next, eternity calls. Such is the fragility of human existence. We make plans, hold conversations, nurse expectations and believe there will always be another day, until life reminds us that tomorrow is never promised.” Calling him the “Lion of Africa,” she said his passing reminded her that “beyond all, the opinions, the misunderstandings and the stories that life sometimes throws around, we are all humans, and death has a way of reminding us of what truly matters.” May also said she would remember Pete as a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contributions to Nollywood would remain unforgettable. “You were an institution, a father figure to many and a man whose legacy will outlive his earthly years,” she wrote. “One thing is certain: legends never truly die; they live on through the memories they create and the impact they leave behind.” She also prayed for Pete’s wife, Josephine, and other relatives, writing: “To mummy and the rest of us you have left behind, may the good Lord strengthen through Christ our Lord.” She ended the tribute with prayers for the deceased: “God rest your soul Ononenyi!” Vanguard News The post ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them. The comedian made the remarks during an appearance on the Charity Zone Podcast, where he argued that the benefits of some government policies might take years to become evident. Seyi Law, a known supporter of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), said economic policies often come with immediate difficulties before producing long term gains. Using China as an example, he said the country’s emergence as a major global economy involved significant sacrifices. “For China to be where they are today, if they tell you the number of Chinese who died, you won’t believe,” he said. When asked whether Nigerians must die before enjoying the benefits of the country’s economic policies, the comedian clarified that people would have to experience the hardship resulting from such decisions before the expected gains could materialise. “No. You must feel the pain of the policy to reap the benefit of it. Every good policy that becomes good stabilises after 10 to 12 years,” he said. Despite his defence of the government, Seyi Law acknowledged the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians, admitting that people were struggling to afford basic necessities. “People are hungry. I will be a hypocrite, a bad person to say people are not hungry,” he said. He also spoke about how the rising cost of living had affected his ability to support family members living in the United Kingdom. According to him, an amount that previously covered their needs now requires a significantly higher sum, forcing him to increase his financial support. “My finances were better before this government came in. My family are in the UK and then with N1.2 million they are okay, but now I have had to double that to like N4.5 million every other month,” he added. nigeria.title: Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football. In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario that he had spoken with the Italian Football Federation but was not ready to take another job. “It was one of the greatest honours I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop,” he said. “If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted.” The Spaniard said the approach came when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom he described as people he loved dearly, reached out to him. He added that he did not know how long his break would last. “Right now I feel very well,” Guardiola told former Brazil forward Romario. “But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.” Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after a decade in charge. He won six Premier League titles, including four in succession, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League. In the same interview, Guardiola said Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry helped prolong both players’ careers. The pair won a combined 13 Ballon d’Or awards and dominated football for more than a decade, including during their spells at Barcelona and Real Madrid. “If Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter,” Guardiola said. “They had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him,’” Guardiola, who coached Messi for four seasons at Barcelona, credited the forward for much of his success there. He led the Spanish club to 14 trophies, including two Champions League titles and three La Liga crowns. “Messi! When you have such good players, you become good yourself,” Guardiola said when asked what helped him win so many titles. nigeria.title: Most Nigerians support political violence when opponents are victims — Shehu Sani
nigeria.description: Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has accused Nigerians of condoning political violence when it is directed at opponents, warning that the attitude is fuelling attacks on political supporters across the country. Sani said many Nigerians encourage violence against people whose political choices or opinions differ from theirs, rather than condemn such acts irrespective of the victims’ affiliations. He stated this on X on Wednesday following the campaign violence that reportedly left four persons dead in Delta State. Condemning the killings, Sani said Nigerians were more likely to support or excuse political violence when those attacked belonged to opposing political camps. “The political violence in Delta State has led to the death of four supporters of Senator Omo Agege of the NDC. A condemnable act. However, we are shying away from the truth that most Nigerians are fully in support of political violence as long as the victims are in the opposite camp,” he wrote. He argued that people who support violence against political opponents often fail to recognise that such acts could eventually affect their own side. “Most people encourage and support mob or thuggish acts against those they differ with in political choices or opinions. Those aiding and abetting political violence are feeding a Tiger with the thought that it will only consume their political adversaries,” Sani said. The former senator also criticised the media’s handling of reports of political attacks, accusing some media organisations of using descriptions that downplay the severity of violence depending on the political affiliation of those involved. He cited reports of attacks involving former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar in Kebbi and President Bola Tinubu in Abuja, saying some media outlets used different descriptions for incidents involving the two political figures. “Some media Houses have even crafted a beautiful way of reporting political violence…POLITICAL THUGS attacked Atiku in Kebbi while ANGRY YOUTHS attacked Tinubu at Abuja Mosque,” he added. Sani’s comments come amid growing concerns over political violence and intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, with incidents involving political supporters raising questions about the safety of campaign activities and the role of political parties in preventing attacks. nigeria.title: Osubi Airport simulates air crash after 20 years
nigeria.description: …Drill identifies emergency response gaps, need for modern equipment By Egufe Yafugborhi WARRI — The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Alfred Diete-Spiff Airport, Osubi, Delta State, has conducted its first simulated aircraft crash rescue exercise in about 20 years to assess its emergency response capabilities and identify areas requiring improvement. The exercise, conducted at about 1:30pm on the airport’s airside, simulated an aircraft crash involving passengers who sustained varying degrees of injuries. Several emergency response agencies participated in the drill, including the Nigerian Navy Hospital and Air Station Fire Service, Nigeria Police Force, Delta State Fire Service, Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Delta Procare Hospital, Nigerian Ports Authority Health Service and Renaissance Africa Energy Fire Service. Speaking after the exercise, the Airport Manager, Winston Egwuatu, expressed satisfaction with the outcome, saying identified operational gaps would be addressed to strengthen the airport’s emergency response capacity. He explained that the exercise was designed to test the preparedness of personnel, availability of equipment and effectiveness of established emergency procedures. “No simulation exercise is perfect. It was actually meant to test the preparedness of both the officers who are going to be deployed, the materials and also the procedures. “The purpose of this is to identify the gaps and close them, so that when it is deployed, we will deploy better,” he said. Egwuatu, who spoke alongside departmental heads, said observers from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) identified areas requiring improvement, particularly personnel training and retraining. He noted that the airport had recorded operational improvements since its transition from an airstrip but stressed the need for additional operational vehicles and modern firefighting equipment. “Within resources available to the management of the airport, we have done very well. This airport used to be an airstrip. Now it’s operating as an airport. That means there have been some level of upgrade. “However, there is need for improvement in regards to operational vehicles and state-of-the-art fire tankers to meet the time that we find ourselves now,” he said. The airport manager disclosed that observations from the exercise would be compiled into a comprehensive report to guide corrective measures and requests requiring intervention from higher authorities. He also emphasised the importance of effective collaboration among emergency response agencies, noting that prompt intervention could determine survival during an aircraft accident. “It is in the interest of everybody to deploy, all of us who have the wherewithal to not just respond, but respond timely. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Wife of the former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has described her husband as the “incoming President of Nigeria” as he turned 80 on Wednesday, saying he is “not tired” and that his vision for the country is “even clearer.” In a birthday tribute titled “Daddy at 80”, Chief Amina Titi Atiku Abubakar, the former Second Lady of Nigeria, said she was celebrating “the Incoming President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria come May 29th, 2027 by the Special Grace of God.” “At 80, you are not tired. At 80, your vision for Nigeria is even clearer. I have walked with you through valleys and mountains, and I know what God has placed in you for Nigeria,” she wrote. She said Nigeria needed his “experience,” his “capacity, and your compassionate heart now more than ever.” According to her, this is “reflecting in the enthusiastic and passionate ways Nigerians turned out to cheer you to victory as you articulate your policies and canvass support for your presidential aspiration come January 16, 2027.” Titi said the milestone coincided with 57 years of marriage. “Eighty years of a life well-lived and Fifty-seven years of a love that has stood the test of time. Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, made the remark in a post on X while thanking Nigerians for their birthday wishes and prayers. He said the nickname was among the names Nigerians had given him that he particularly enjoyed, adding that he remained committed to making life easier for citizens. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon,” he wrote. Despite their differences in political affiliation and views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability remained important. nigeria.title: Reps order contractor back to failed East-west road culverts
nigeria.description: …Demand urgent repairs, four-week monitoring of project By Gift Chapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Ministry of Works to direct Rock Result Nigeria Limited to return immediately to the site and rehabilitate or reconstruct damaged box culverts along the East-West Road, particularly at Iheke in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Hon. Oboku Abonsizibe Oforji, who drew the attention of lawmakers to the reported deterioration of the culverts and the need for urgent intervention to prevent further damage and potential safety risks. The House recalled that it had, on October 3, 2023, adopted a motion on the deplorable condition of the East-West Road, particularly the Iheke axis, following which the Federal Government undertook further interventions. The interventions included the construction of box culverts, approval and release of funds for rehabilitation and flood mitigation works, payments to Rock Result Nigeria Limited and the re-award of the contract to Setraco Nigeria Limited for the continuation of the road dualisation project. However, lawmakers expressed concern over reports that the constructed box culverts had deteriorated, despite the financial commitments made by the government. They said the reported condition of the drainage infrastructure underscored the need for a technical assessment of the works, including the materials used, construction standards and supervision of the project. The House noted that the East-West Road was a major economic and social corridor connecting Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta states to other parts of the country, serving communities and facilitating the movement of people, goods and services. It warned that the deteriorating condition of the road could further disrupt transportation and expose motorists and other road users to safety risks. Lawmakers also expressed concern that the dualisation of the East-West Road from Ahoada in Rivers State through the Bayelsa axis to Patani in Delta State remained incomplete, despite earlier completion targets of April 2025 and November 2025. Consequently, the House urged the Ministry of Works to ensure that Rock Result Nigeria Limited returned to the site without delay to carry out the required rehabilitation or reconstruction of the damaged culverts in accordance with approved engineering standards. It also called for adequate technical supervision, quality assurance and an independent engineering assessment of the remedial works to reduce the risk of further structural problems. In addition, the lawmakers urged the ministry to ensure the completion of the dualisation of the Ahoada-Bayelsa and Patani sections of the road by Setraco Nigeria Limited. The House mandated its Committee on Works and Legislative Compliance to monitor the implementation of the resolutions and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. nigeria.description: …Protest over unpaid allowances, give management until Thursday By Adesina Wahab Non-teaching staff of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, on Wednesday protested the non-payment of several allowances owed them, threatening to embark on an indefinite strike from Thursday if their demands were not met. The workers, under the umbrella of the Non-Teaching Staff Union of Polytechnics (NOTSUP), staged a protest march around the campus, led by the union’s Branch Chairman, Bayo Sanusi. They marched to the Administrative Block, which houses the Rector’s office, the Bursary Department and the institution’s main gate, singing solidarity songs and displaying placards bearing various messages. Addressing the protesters, Sanusi expressed displeasure over what he described as the exclusion of non-teaching staff from the payment of allowances, despite the reported payment of similar entitlements to teaching staff. He said teaching and non-teaching employees played complementary roles in the administration of tertiary institutions and should be treated fairly. “I don’t know whether our people have seen a bird flying with one wing. It is not possible. Tertiary institutions like ours have teaching and non-teaching staff and we complement one another. NOTSUP is made up of NASU and SSANIP members and we are united in calling for the payment of our dues. A labourer, they say, is worth his wages,” he said. Sanusi said the union’s national leadership had engaged the Federal Government on the outstanding allowances and reached an agreement on their payment. He added that the Minister of Education had directed the managements of federal polytechnics and colleges of education to source funds for the payments from available resources, including savings from capital expenditure and internally generated revenue, with a promise that the Federal Government would reimburse the institutions. According to him, at least three federal polytechnics had complied with the directive and paid the allowances, while non-teaching staff at YABATECH were still awaiting payment. He said the union had engaged the college management and was assured last Wednesday that the outstanding entitlements would be paid, but the promise had yet to be fulfilled. “In line with the directive by the Minister, at least three federal Polytechnics have paid. Here at YABATECH, teaching staff have been paid leaving us in the lurch like orphans. We are not less human than teaching staff. nigeria.title: Reps seek clarification over mining marshals’ letter to lawmaker
nigeria.description: …Give NSCDC seven days to submit operational records By Gift Cnapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals Development has asked the Commander of the Mining Marshals, ACC Attah John Onoja, to tender a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of a letter concerning a member of the House, Hon. Abdulmalik Danga. The committee also gave the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) seven days to submit outstanding operational records relating to petitions on the activities of the Mining Marshals, including complaints about arrests, detention of mining operators and the closure of mining sites. The decisions followed an investigative hearing chaired by Hon. Jonathan Gaza, during which lawmakers sought clarification from Onoja over a July 24, 2026 letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas. The letter concerned the intervention of Danga, who represents Adavi/Okehi Federal Constituency of Kogi State, in matters relating to the activities of the Mining Marshals. In the correspondence, Onoja expressed reservations about the lawmaker’s intervention, linking it to concerns surrounding the enforcement of regulations against illegal mining. Reading an excerpt from the letter, Gaza said the language used in the correspondence raised concerns about the manner in which a serving member of the National Assembly was addressed. The letter stated: “While we respect the rules of lawmaking in shaping the society through oversight legislative functions, we strongly view the action of Abdulmalik Danga as anti-government and motivated by illegal mining cartels whose unlawful activities are being disrupted by the sanity being restored in the mining sector.” The committee members questioned the basis for the assertions and whether the correspondence reflected an authorised institutional position of the NSCDC. Responding, Onoja told the committee that he wrote the letter in his personal capacity as Commander of the Mining Marshals and did not intend to challenge the constitutional powers of the legislature. He said: “Mr. Chairman, permit me to state clearly on record. My response, my letter, in my personal capacity as the Commander Mining Marshals, is not in any way looking into the legislative powers of the Committee. The letter is speaking to the motion as moved.” Gaza, however, questioned the explanation, particularly because the correspondence was written on NSCDC letterhead and carried an official reference number. The committee chairman consequently asked the NSCDC Commandant-General, Ahmed Abubakar Audi, to clarify whether the letter represented the official position of the Corps or was issued without institutional authorisation. nigeria.title: ₦1.45trn Lagos ports upgrade targets 20,000 jobs
nigeria.description: …As FG flags off Apapa, Tin Can modernisation By Efe Onodjae The Federal Government on Wednesday flagged off a £746 million (about ₦1.45 trillion) modernisation of Apapa and Tin Can Island ports in Lagos, targeting 48-hour cargo clearance and the creation of 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The project is expected to reduce cargo delays, lower logistics costs and improve Nigeria’s competitiveness in global trade. Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Adegboyega Oyetola, who performed the groundbreaking at Tin Can Island Port, said the upgrade had become urgent as cargo throughput had outgrown existing port infrastructure. Oyetola said Nigeria’s cargo throughput had increased from 8.11 million metric tonnes in 1977 to 129.3 million metric tonnes, while merchandise trade had risen from $17 billion to over $100 billion annually. He said the project would involve rehabilitation of quay walls and berths, dredging of navigation channels, improved access facilities and installation of modern cargo-handling equipment. According to him, cargo dwell time at Nigerian ports had historically ranged between 10 and 18 days, compared with three to five days at leading international ports, costing the economy an estimated $4 billion annually. He said the upgrade would attract international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo and expand transshipment opportunities. Also speaking, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, described the project as Nigeria’s largest sovereign export credit transaction since 2009. He said the financing arrangement demonstrated international investor confidence in Nigeria’s economic reforms. Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, assured that the project would be delivered in line with approved designs, engineering standards and contractual timelines. nigeria.title: Tinubu pledges to rescue abducted Borno schoolchildren
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri MAIDUGURI — President Bola Tinubu has pledged that his administration will do everything possible to secure the release of about 70 schoolchildren abducted from Mussa Primary School and Government Technical School, Lassa, in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State. Tinubu made the pledge on Wednesday in Maiduguri while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-East Zonal Rally held at the El-Kanemi Sports Centre. The President said his administration remained committed to rescuing the children abducted by suspected Boko Haram terrorists and defeating insurgency in the North-East. “We shall do everything possible to rescue the schoolchildren abducted in Mussa and Lassa communities,” he said. The abductions, which occurred in the first quarter of 2026, involved more than 30 children, including toddlers, from Mussa and over 40 students from Lassa. Tinubu also acknowledged the sacrifices of military personnel and other security operatives, particularly those serving on the frontline, assuring them of government support in the fight against terrorism. “The present administration under my leadership acknowledges the sacrifices of troops, especially those at the frontline. Therefore, government would do its best to support our security operatives to defeat terrorism in this region,” he said. On his second-term ambition, the President thanked the people of the North-East for their support for the APC-led administration, promising to consolidate on its achievements if re-elected in 2027. He described Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who hails from Borno State, as a dependable ally and commended Governor Babagana Zulum for his administration’s development efforts. Tinubu particularly cited the newly constructed International Conference Centre in Maiduguri and other projects he commissioned during his visit. Earlier, Zulum thanked the President for choosing Maiduguri as the venue for the zonal rally, expressing satisfaction with the large turnout and orderly conduct of APC supporters. He said Borno State had benefited significantly from the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda. The governor disclosed that the Federal Government had commenced construction of the Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri road, while also highlighting the establishment of the Federal Polytechnic, Monguno; Federal College of Education, Gwoza; and Federal University of Agriculture and Entrepreneurship, Bama. Zulum urged residents of Borno and other states in the North-East to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. The rally attracted seven governors from the region, including Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State. Also in attendance were the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu; wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima; former governors; ministers; members of the National Assembly and other APC stakeholders. nigeria.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
nigeria.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. business.title: France’s Senate Rejects Rule Forcing Bitcoin Holders to Declare Self-Custody Wallets
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine France’s Senate Rejects Rule Forcing Bitcoin Holders to Declare Self-Custody Wallets France’s Senate has rejected a proposal that would have forced bitcoin holders to report self-custody wallets worth €100,000 or more to the tax authorities, along with two other crypto tax measures in the 2027 budget. Senators voted down two identical amendments on Nov. 24 during debate on the first part of the 2027 finance bill. Both would have required taxpayers to declare crypto wallets they hold directly, outside a crypto service provider, when the total value inside reached at least €100,000 on Dec. 31 of the tax year. The first, amendment I-2447 , came from Sens. Pascal Savoldelli and Pierre Barros and the Communist-led CRCE-K group. The second, amendment I-2992 , came from Sen. Anne-Sophie Romagny and seven other senators. The government opposed both, and both were rejected. The case for a wallet rule in France Backers argued that France already makes taxpayers declare accounts on foreign crypto platforms, just like foreign bank accounts. Wallets that holders manage themselves, without an intermediary, escape any such obligation. “They have become the digital equivalent of the undeclared safe,” the CRCE-K group wrote in its amendment, adding that tax authorities can’t see them, check gains on them or reach them in an estate or when a holder moves abroad. Romagny’s version pointed to a gap in the numbers. Crypto holders in France realized €3.5 billion in gains in 2021, but only €400 million in digital assets were declared to the tax administration that same year, the amendment said. It proposed fines of up to €10,000 for failing to declare. The National Assembly had approved the same wallet rule on Nov. 3. It fell away the next day, when deputies rejected the entire revenue section of the budget. Senators then took up the same measure as an amendment to the budget. Stablecoin swaps and exit tax also rejected Senators also rejected two other proposals from the CRCE-K group. Amendment I-2421 would have ended France’s tax deferral on swaps into electronic money tokens under the EU’s MiCA rules. That would have made converting bitcoin into a regulated stablecoin a taxable event. Amendment I-2428 would have pulled crypto into France’s exit tax on unrealized gains for people who move their tax home abroad. It counted all crypto toward the €800,000 threshold, including coins held in self-custody or outside France. David Amiel, France’s minister for public action and accounts, argued against the wallet rule, saying the EU’s DAC8 directive already puts reporting duties on crypto firms. He said he was “more circumspect” about a “purely declarative” obligation that would not help authorities track crypto used in money laundering or tax fraud. The Senate’s finance committee also opposed the measures, and rapporteur general Christine Lavarde recommended rejecting all three. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Either way, the Yankees just gained a player who knows how to get outs in the playoffs. The $4 million price tag reflects his value. They needed depth after a long season, and Suter provides exactly that. For Atlanta, the loss is not just about the numbers. It is about the stability he offered in a bullpen that often gets tested. sports.title: What Peugeot had planned for its abandoned 2027 WEC Hypercar
sports.description: Motorsport photo The 2027-spec 9X8 LMH was set to offer Peugeot its best chance of becoming a consistent World Endurance Championship frontrunner against some stiff Hypercar competition. The French manufacturer had invested considerable resources into developing a revised version of the car that had fallen short of the expectations set by its predecessor, the 908 LMP1. This would have been the third major iteration of the V6-powered challenger, following a previous update in 2024 that failed to yield the desired results. By mid-2025, Peugeot had already identified several key weaknesses with the package. Even after being granted the lowest weight and the maximum power under the Balance of Performance adjustments, the 9X8 was simply not competitive enough against the likes of Toyota, Porsche and Ferrari . Peugeot felt that incremental refinements alone would not be enough, with the car having reached a performance ceiling that engineers struggled to overcome. While Peugeot initially considered ditching the 9X8 entirely in favour of a clean-sheet design, even holding talks with the WEC’s promoters – to understand if this would be allowed, it eventually chose to update its existing car instead. The French manufacturer had its hands tied in 2026, having already exhausted its original allocation of five evo jokers and the second homologation. So it spent the year struggling largely at the back of the pack, while its engineers simultaneously began working on overhauling the package for 2027, with a new rule granting struggling manufacturers two additional evo updates during their cars' life cycles. Crucially, the update Peugeot had planned for 2027 wasn’t about undoing the damage caused by the convergence of the LMH and LMDh regulations – something that had significantly compromised the original design of the car. Instead, it was aimed at tackling the specific shortcomings of the second-generation 9X8, including its notoriously poor performance at the Le Mans 24 Hours. As with other manufacturers introducing evo updates, aerodynamics was the key focus of development for the Satory-based brand. But it was also working on several other changes under the hood to improve the cornering performance of the 9X8. #94 Peugeot Totalenergies Peugeot 9X8: Loic Duval #94 Peugeot Totalenergies Peugeot 9X8: Loic Duval “In terms of development of the car, the key targets were to eradicate the issues we had with the current package,” team principal Emmanuel Esnault explained at Monza earlier this month. “So, meaning in terms of [aero] dumping [to improve straightline performance] and in terms of aero consistency; these were the key words. “The main handicaps we had were the aerodynamic balance variation on the three phases that make up a corner; that is the entry, the middle of the corner and the exit. “And the [other area of focus was] control of the platform, which is the damping of the suspension. sports.description: Confirmed: Fermin Lopez hit with two-match ban; will miss Deportivo, Atletico Madrid games In what comes as a blow for Barcelona, key midfielder Fermin Lopez has been hit with a two-match suspension following his red card against Villarreal last Sunday. As a result, the in-form 23-year-old will miss the team’s La Liga matches against Deportivo de A Coruna and Atletico Madrid over the coming week. What happened? Fermin was sent off by referee Hernandez Hernandez while being seated on the Barcelona bench in the second half during the 3-2 win over Villarreal. It emanated from the La Masia graduate, who had scored on the day before being subbed off, voicing his protest over a potential penalty decision not going the Catalans’ way for a foul on Anthony Gordon. Fermin was sent off against Villarreal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The referee recorded the incident in his report, stating that the midfielder had left the dugout and approached the fourth official at close range while protesting loudly. The referee specifically noted that Fermin repeatedly used the expression “Don’t f**k with me!” during the exchange. Two-match ban Barcelona were hoping that the youngster would get away with only a one-match suspension. However, the Disciplinary Committee has classified the incident as a protest under Article 127 of the Disciplinary Code. The regulation provides for a suspension of between two and three matches, or a ban of up to one month, for protesting against the referee, assistant referees or fourth official when the conduct does not constitute a more serious offence. Two-match ban for Fermin. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Fermin has now received the minimum suspension under the article: two matches. Barcelona had submitted an appeal in an attempt to challenge the decision, but they were not accepted. The suspension means the midfielder will be unavailable for Barcelona’s visit to Deportivo at Riazor this Sunday. The more significant absence comes next Wednesday, when Barcelona host Atletico Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou – a fixture that was initially scheduled for January but brought forward due to the Spanish Super Cup scheduling. Barcelona have little room to challenge the decision successfully through the Appeals Committee as the disciplinary body has imposed the lowest punishment available under the relevant regulation, which makes the prospect of reducing the suspension limited. sports.description: On December 1, 2001, my Bowie High School team beat Eleanor Roosevelt 23-6 at Byrd Stadium for the first state championship in school history. We were the sixth seed. Roosevelt was undefeated and had beaten us in September. They had won nine straight against us, going back to 1994. We scored the first 23 points. When it was over, one of my teammates walked off that field with a plastic bag full of grass—a souvenir. I got home late that night. My parents were proud, but they kept it simple: Be safe, and be home when we wake up. The next morning, I was in church. I even got a shout-out from the pulpit. And that afternoon, I was in the yard cutting the grass, because the playoff run had put me behind on my chores. Took me years to understand it, but the trophy and the lawnmower were the same lesson. The habits that won the championship were the same ones that had me cutting grass the next day. Sunday night in Mexico City was the 49ers’ championship night. A 35-10 win over the best defense in football, in prime time, on an international stage. By Monday, they were Super Bowl favorites, and Brock Purdy’s MVP odds had jumped from +400 to +210. Then Kyle Shanahan was asked if this is the best team he’s coached in San Francisco. “No, but it’s still early,” he said. “We’ve got to earn that.” Now it’s back to the yard. It’s been 49 days since the 49ers played a division game, and the last one took just about everything they had. Seven turnovers between the two teams. Six lead changes. The 49ers hadn’t scored a touchdown against Seattle in more than eight quarters until Mike Evans caught a 2-yarder less than four minutes in. Renardo Green picked off Sam Darnold twice. Fred Warner punched a ball loose, Malik Mustapha fell on it, and Christian McCaffrey scored on the next snap. With 13 seconds left in the half, G-Baby, rookie Gracen Halton, stripped George Holani and recovered it in the end zone. Then Seattle scored 13 straight in the third quarter, and the 49ers had to go get it. Down 26-21, they went 74 yards in 12 plays, and Evans caught a 28-yarder on second-and-21 to set up the go-ahead touchdown. The winning field goal came at the end of a drive built on five runs for 36 yards, and Seattle’s last shot died when Cooper Kupp came up short on fourth-and-10 at midfield. That’s what the division looks like. Ugly, physical, and decided by inches. And the 49ers walking into Levi’s on Sunday aren’t the same team that left Seattle. sports.title: Man behind the curtain calling entertainment plays at Polar Park
sports.description: WORCESTER – While fans watch the players sweep through the field, sing along to classics and new hits, and wait for their sick moves to appear on the jumbotron, there is a man sitting behind a curtain making it all happen. Actually, there are several. Many people go to the ballpark to watch the game, but it is not the only interesting thing happening there. From music to the kiss cam, the Worcester Red Sox Entertainment Department helps turn baseball into a full night out at Polar Park. Without the technology that has become a regular part of the modern-day ballpark experience, this job would look significantly different. Before video boards became a regular feature, scoreboards were used for the minimum: the score, the inning and the lineup. That changed in 1980 when Dodger Stadium introduced the first full-color video board during the All-Star Game. This technology opened up new opportunities for entertainment beyond the game. Over time, video boards brought replays, highlights, promotional videos and crowd-participation features. According to Fun While it Lasted, a website that documents the history of sports, when the Pawtucket Red Sox – rebranded as the Worcester Red Sox – moved to Worcester in 2021, the franchise significantly stepped up its technology game. Polar Park was built with five boards, including two large video screens. It was a huge change from McCoy Stadium, which had been referred to as “a dump” by Ben Mondor, a retired mill owner who became the Pawtucket Red Sox’s third owner in the '70s. Westborough native at the controls For Brendan Black, a longtime baseball fan who grew up in Westborough, those large screens were wildly important. He is the director of ballpark entertainment. Black began working for the team in 2021 as a videographer before moving into a producer role in 2023. His job took root at age 10, when he was first interested in photography and videography, eventually teaching himself how to edit videos. After studying communications at the University of New Hampshire, he found himself working in sales to pay the bills. It was a relief when the WooSox came along, opening up an opportunity for him. “It just so happened that these two worlds of mine kind of collided,” Black said, recalling what it was like to bring together two interests that had followed him for years – baseball and entertainment. But putting on a show takes more than making a playlist and pressing "play." On game days, the work begins long before the fans fill the seats. At 10 a.m., the team holds what Black calls a “DOG” meeting – short for Day of Game. The staff goes over the weather, expected crowd size, ticket blocks and any promotions planned. sports.title: John Motson’s legendary voice resurrected by AI for EA FC 27
sports.description: Legendary football commentator John Motson‘s voice is set to return to EA FC 27 through the use of AI - three years after his death. Motson, who died aged 77 in 2023 , worked on the BBC ’s flagship Match of the Day programme since 1971 and covered more than 2,000 televised games, including 29 FA Cup finals and 10 World Cups. He retired from live commentary in 2008 but continued to work on Match of the Day programme until he hung up the microphone in 2018. EA Sports said they worked with John Motson’s family to bring back his iconic voice in a “digital tribute” through the use of new AI-tools, “bringing a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself”. The commentator featured in EA Sports’ annual FIFA game series from 1996 to 2006. John Motson featured in EA Sports’ annual FIFA game series from 1996 to 2006 A studio spokesperson said EA Sports have “worked with extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game’s greatest voices, inspiring a whole new generation of football fans.” “My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,” said Fred Motson, son of John Motson. “His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.” After starting as a newspaper reporter in Barnet and at the Sheffield Morning Telegraph , Motson joined the BBC in 1968 as a sports presenter on Radio 2. His long career also took in two Olympic Games and Wimbledon’s memorable 1988 FA Cup final triumph against Liverpool at Wembley, as the Crazy Gang beat the Culture Club. Awarded the OBE in 2001 for services to broadcasting, Motson hung up his microphone for the BBC at the end of the 2017-18 Premier League season. EA Sports football game series began in 1994 with the release of FIFA International Soccer, with the FIFA name continuing until 2023, when the termination of EA and FIFA’s licensing agreement led to the 2024 game being called FC. John Motson’s voice will be added to EA in Title Update v1.3.0 on 26 November as an optional commentary selection.
